title: Chicken pot pie
subtitle: Creamy chicken and vegetable filling under a golden puff pastry lid
excerpt: Chicken pot pie is a chicken and vegetable filling in a thick cream sauce, baked under a puff pastry lid until the top is golden and the filling bubbles at the edges. It is made in a deep pie dish and takes about an hour start to finish. One of the great American comfort dishes.
sourceNotes: American home-cooking tradition. Chicken pot pie in its covered-pastry form appears in Fannie Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896), Project Gutenberg. The modern deep-dish version with puff pastry became standard in mid-twentieth century American home cookbooks.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble unbaked and freeze. Bake from frozen at 190°C for 50 to 60 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made a day ahead and refrigerated. Assemble with the pastry lid and bake just before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cooked mixture of equal parts butter and flour used to thicken sauces. The butter is melted, the flour added and stirred over heat for a minute or two, then liquid is added gradually.

content.text: Chicken pot pie starts with a butter-and-flour

enriched with stock and cream, loaded with poached chicken and vegetables, then covered with a sheet of puff pastry and baked until the filling bubbles and the top is deep gold. It is forgiving: the filling holds well and the pastry lid is the only delicate part.

items.prepNote: poached and shredded, or use leftover roast chicken

content.text: Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the {{onion}} onion, {{carrot}} carrots, and {{celery}} celery. Cook for 6 minutes until softened. Add {{plain-flour}} of flour and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes.

Gradually whisk in {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock, adding it in stages to avoid lumps. Add {{thyme}} sprigs of thyme and {{bay-leaves}} of bay. Simmer for 10 minutes until thickened. Remove the thyme and bay. Stir in {{double-cream}} of double cream, the shredded chicken, and {{peas-frozen}} of peas. Season well. Leave to cool slightly.

Heat the oven to 200°C. Pour the filling into the pie dish. Lay the {{puff-pastry}} of puff pastry sheet over the top, pressing it to the edges. Trim the excess. Cut two small slits in the top to let steam escape. Brush with the beaten egg.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.cause: Filling too hot when the pastry went on, or filling too liquid.
items.fix: Cool the filling to at least warm before adding the pastry lid. Thicken the sauce further before filling the dish.

items.symptom: Filling bubbling out around the edges
items.cause: Dish too full, or pastry not properly sealed to the rim.
items.fix: Press the pastry firmly to the dish rim and trim cleanly. Do not overfill: leave 2 cm below the pastry.

items.cause: Not enough flour in the roux, or too much stock added.
items.fix: The sauce should coat a spoon thickly before the pastry goes on. If thin, simmer for a further 5 minutes.

content.text: Turkey pot pie is the classic Thanksgiving-leftovers version: swap the chicken for leftover roast turkey. Adding a handful of chestnut mushrooms to the filling makes it more substantial. Shortcrust pastry in place of puff gives a denser, more traditional lid. Individual pies in deep ramekins make a smart dinner-party starter.

Chicken pot pie is one of the most reliably comforting dishes in the American home-cooking repertoire. It has been on American dinner tables since the colonial period, when it followed the British pasty and pie tradition brought by the first settlers. The deep-dish version with a single pastry lid became standard in the mid-twentieth century.
